types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a customer does not make it a different customer; a value invariant across all of a customer's dated statements is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's customer number is never reassigned to a different customer; if a customer number were reused for a different customer this role would misidentify statements, which should trigger review.
types.review_trigger: the same customer_number value appears to identify two customers the business considers different

types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to an account does not make it a different account; a value invariant across all of an account's dated statements is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's account number is never reassigned to a different account; if an account number were reused for a different account this role would misidentify statements, which should trigger review.
types.review_trigger: the same account_number value appears to identify two accounts the business considers different

types.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept beside the statement, and L1.as-of requires ordering statements by that moment to answer any as-of question; a dedicated effective-time value is indispensable to both. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is exactly the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while every statement's effective moment can be determined at all; where a source supplies no moment of its own, this value cannot yet be assigned and as-of answers for that statement are unavailable.
types.review_trigger: a statement is recorded with no determinable effective moment, or two statements of the same identity report the same moment

types.necessity: L1.current-version defines the current statement as the one with no later statement and requires exactly one per customer or account; a flag recording that fact is indispensable to expose it without recomputation. It is a fact about that dated statement relative to the others, never edited in place on an existing statement, which is the per_statement mutation role, not mutable.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible as long as effective moments are known and ordered for every statement of a thing; if effective moments are missing, the current flag cannot be determined either.
types.review_trigger: more than one or zero statements of the same identity are flagged current

types.necessity: L1.deletion-withdraws requires that a withdrawal report take its place in the order of reports like any other report, yet from its moment forward the record has no standing; a dedicated flag distinguishing a withdrawal statement from an ordinary standing statement is indispensable to express that distinction without recomputing it ad hoc wherever current-ness or as-of answers are checked. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while a withdrawal is carried only by a source's own delete signal (a customer or account CDC record's cdc_flag); where the source that could carry that signal supplies no effective-time handoff to a versioned entity, no statement of this job can yet be marked withdrawn, so every statement it currently produces has this flag false. Should the deferred CDC handoffs ever be undeferred, this type's role stays the same and no revisit is required by that alone.
types.review_trigger: a statement is found for which is_withdrawal cannot be determined from its producing source, or a withdrawal statement is found to carry a non-null standing fact

types.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing, and L1.statement-content names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account's dated statement carries; the account's statement must therefore carry which customer it belongs to so that customer's as-of statement can be found for the same moment. This value belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while every account statement's owning customer is knowable at the moment the statement is recorded; whether a change to the owner alone creates a new account statement is unresolved.
types.review_trigger: an account statement has no resolvable owning customer, or the owner recorded contradicts the customer entity's identity values

types.necessity: the clause requires any constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears and never mixed into received records; a dedicated provenance value is indispensable to carry that label through the model. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while every constructed scenario is loaded only through its labeled source and every received record is loaded only through raw sources.
types.review_trigger: a statement sourced from a raw feed carries a constructed label, or a statement sourced from a labeled constructed feed carries none

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'whether the customer is active or inactive' as part of the standing facts a customer's dated statement carries; a dedicated status value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact, distinct from tier. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding distinguishes exactly active and inactive states for a customer at the moment of a statement; a source that reports additional intermediate states would require this type to be reassessed.
types.review_trigger: a source reports a customer status value that is neither active nor inactive, or a customer statement has no determinable status where the clause requires one

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'the customer's tier' as part of the standing facts a customer's dated statement carries; a dedicated tier value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tier value per customer statement, consistent with a per_statement fact rather than a running total.
types.review_trigger: a customer statement reports more than one tier value, or a tier value outside the brokerage's known tier range

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'whether the account is open or closed' as part of the standing facts an account's dated statement carries; a dedicated status value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact, distinct from tax treatment and ownership.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding distinguishes exactly open and closed states for an account at the moment of a statement.
types.review_trigger: a source reports an account status value that is neither open nor closed, or an account statement has no determinable status where the clause requires one

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'its tax treatment' as part of the standing facts an account's dated statement carries; a dedicated tax-treatment value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax-treatment value per account statement, consistent with a per_statement fact.
types.review_trigger: an account statement reports more than one tax-treatment value, or a value outside the brokerage's known tax-treatment codes

entities.grain: one dated statement about one customer, holding from its effective moment until superseded by a later statement of the same customer
entities.necessity: L1.identity requires the customer to be a persistent identified thing rather than a row that changes identity; L1.history requires every change kept beside the earlier one with its effective moment; L1.as-of requires the kept statements be ordered so any moment resolves to one of them — together these entail a versioned entity of dated statements about one identified customer. The single-current-statement requirement and the standing facts each statement carries are further specified, at the attribute level, by L1.current-version and L1.statement-content respectively.
entities.parallel_assumption: Credible while every recorded change to a customer is delivered as a new statement rather than an overwrite of a prior one.
entities.review_trigger: a customer's prior statement is found overwritten rather than superseded by a new one

attributes.name: customer_number
attributes.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which customer a statement is about and stays the same across that customer's changes; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's customer number is stable and unique per customer.
attributes.review_trigger: two statements with different customer_number values are claimed to be about the same customer, or vice versa

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept with the statement; L1.as-of requires that moment to determine which statement answers a query as of any time.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own moment of change; not yet derivable for incremental customer change records.
attributes.review_trigger: a customer statement has no source-supplied moment of change

attributes.name: is_current

derivation.rule: false when this statement's own is_withdrawal is true, since a withdrawal statement is never itself the current one; false when a withdrawal statement of the same customer_number has an effective_from at or before this statement's effective_from, since a statement dated at or after a withdrawal is not treated as resuming the withdrawn record's standing, per L1.hole.deletion-reversal's 'until answered, no job may treat a report received after a withdrawal as resuming the record' -- this holds even when that later statement is itself an ordinary, ostensibly non-withdrawal report; otherwise true when no statement of the same customer_number has a later effective_from than this one and false when one does. It follows that once a customer has any withdrawal statement, no statement of that customer_number at or after the withdrawal's own moment is ever current again, pending L1.hole.deletion-reversal, and, within that bound, at most one statement is current per L1.current-version's amendment ('none once its latest statement is a withdrawal'). Not received from any source.

attributes.necessity: L1.current-version requires at most one current statement per customer, defined as the one with no later statement, and none once the latest statement is a withdrawal; this attribute exposes that fact directly. L1.hole.deletion-reversal forbids treating a report received after a withdrawal as resuming the record, so this attribute's derivation must foreclose currency from the withdrawal's own moment forward rather than merely at the withdrawal statement itself, or a later ordinary report would silently answer the hole by resuming the record.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible once every customer statement has a known effective_from to order it against the others and a known is_withdrawal value. The withdrawal branch, and the reversal-foreclosure branch it now requires, are not yet exercised by this job: every statement it currently produces has is_withdrawal false (see the is_withdrawal attribute), because the sources that could set it true remain deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time. Should a report ever be received after a withdrawal, this rule reads it as not resuming the record, matching trade-lifecycle's monotonic treatment of the same hole for a trade's withdrawn flag; if the business answers L1.hole.deletion-reversal to allow resumption, this derivation must be revisited.
attributes.review_trigger: zero or more than one statement of the same customer_number is flagged current, a statement with is_withdrawal true is flagged current, or a statement dated at or after a withdrawal of the same customer_number is flagged current

attributes.name: is_withdrawal

derivation.rule: false for every statement produced by raw.customer_mgmt_action, whose action_type vocabulary (NEW, UPDCUST, INACT) names no withdrawal action at all; true for a statement produced by a customer CDC record whose cdc_flag is D, per the deferred handoff below, since L1.deletion-withdraws holds that such a report withdraws the brokerage's assertion of the customer from its own moment rather than stating an ordinary change; false for one whose cdc_flag is I or U, an ordinary insert or update. A customer CDC record whose cdc_flag is outside the anchored {I, U, D} vocabulary is not read as false by this rule: per L1.unknown-codes, that record is held for review and no fact, including is_withdrawal, is derived from it at all, so this attribute is not populated for it rather than defaulting to false.

attributes.necessity: L1.deletion-withdraws requires the model to distinguish a withdrawal report from an ordinary statement so that current-ness, as-of answers, and standing-fact content can each treat it differently as the clause requires; this attribute is that distinction, carried per statement.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible for statements sourced from raw.customer_mgmt_action, whose action_type vocabulary has no withdrawal action, so is_withdrawal is always determinable as false there. Not yet exercisable for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer CDC record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; until it is undeferred, this job produces no statement with is_withdrawal true, which is the honest, unexercised state of this attribute rather than a silent default.
attributes.review_trigger: the change-effective-time hole is resolved and the deferred cdc_flag handoff can be promoted from deferred to candidate, or a statement is found with an indeterminate is_withdrawal value

attributes.name: status
attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry whether the customer is active or inactive; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. A withdrawal statement carries no standing fact at all, per L1.deletion-withdraws, so it must not populate this attribute either.
attributes.note: Non-null for every non-withdrawal statement, checked by inv.customer_statement_has_content; null for a statement whose is_withdrawal is true, since L1.deletion-withdraws holds a withdrawal creates nothing and asserts no standing, so it must not be read as active or inactive.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its active/inactive fact directly, or entails it through a stated code meaning: the historical action file entails it through the anchored meaning of action_type (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive), and an incremental customer change record supplies it directly through c_st_id, though the latter's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time). No source this job reads today produces a withdrawal statement at all, so the null branch is not yet exercised.
attributes.review_trigger: a customer statement is recorded with no determinable active/inactive fact from a source that is expected to supply or entail one, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null status

attributes.name: tier

derivation.rule: When the action producing this statement omits the customer's tier field (as INACT does; see sources-v1.json action_type_meanings.fields_present), L1.omitted-facts-stand holds that the omitted fact stands as it last stood: tier equals the value carried by this customer's immediately preceding statement. L1.identity holds that a change produces a new dated statement about the same customer, not a different one, and L1.history holds that a later statement sits beside the earlier one rather than overwriting it, so 'the immediately preceding statement of this customer' is well defined. A preceding statement is guaranteed to exist here: INACT's anchored meaning ('a customer becomes inactive') presupposes an existing customer, since only NEW first records a customer, so an INACT row is never a customer's first statement.

attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. Where the producing action omits this field (as INACT does), this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history. A withdrawal statement carries no standing fact at all, per L1.deletion-withdraws, so the carried-forward derivation does not apply to it either.
attributes.note: Non-null for every non-withdrawal statement (directly supplied or carried forward), checked by inv.customer_statement_has_content; null for a statement whose is_withdrawal is true, since a withdrawal asserts no standing to carry forward or otherwise.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own tier fact directly, or, when the producing action omits it, per the carried-forward derivation; credible while an action's omission of tier is understood to mean the fact is unchanged rather than unknown. The preceding statement this derivation carries from is itself sourced from the historical action file only while incremental customer CDC content handoffs stay deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; should they be promoted to candidate, this derivation must be revisited for how it identifies the immediately preceding statement. No source this job reads today produces a withdrawal statement, so the null branch is not yet exercised.
attributes.review_trigger: a customer statement has no determinable tier value from a source that is expected to supply or carry it forward, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null tier

entities.grain: one dated statement about one account, holding from its effective moment until superseded by a later statement of the same account
entities.necessity: L1.identity, L1.history, and L1.as-of require the same versioned-and-identified shape as the customer entity: a persistent identified account with dated, kept, orderable statements. The single-current-statement requirement, the owning-customer link, and the standing facts each statement carries are further specified, at the attribute level, by L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, and L1.statement-content respectively.
entities.parallel_assumption: Credible while every recorded change to an account is delivered as a new statement rather than an overwrite of a prior one.
entities.review_trigger: an account's prior statement is found overwritten rather than superseded by a new one

attributes.name: account_number
attributes.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which account a statement is about and stays the same across that account's changes; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's account number is stable and unique per account.
attributes.review_trigger: two statements with different account_number values are claimed to be about the same account, or vice versa

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept with the statement; L1.as-of requires that moment to determine which statement answers a query as of any time.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own moment of change; not yet derivable for incremental account change records.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement has no source-supplied moment of change

attributes.name: is_current

derivation.rule: false when this statement's own is_withdrawal is true, since a withdrawal statement is never itself the current one; false when a withdrawal statement of the same account_number has an effective_from at or before this statement's effective_from, since a statement dated at or after the account's own withdrawal is not treated as resuming it, per L1.hole.deletion-reversal, even when that later statement is itself an ordinary report; false when this statement's own owning_customer_number's customer entity has a withdrawal statement with an effective_from at or before this statement's effective_from, since L1.owner-standing's extended second sentence holds that an account has no standing at a moment when its owner has none, and this attribute is the compiled form of that cascade rather than a fact asserted only by an invariant with nothing producing it; otherwise true when no statement of the same account_number has a later effective_from than this one and false when one does. It follows that once an account's own record or its owning customer's record carries a withdrawal, no statement of that account_number at or after the earlier of the two withdrawal moments is ever current again, pending L1.hole.deletion-reversal for the account's own case, and, within that bound, at most one statement is current per L1.current-version's amendment. Not received from any source.

attributes.necessity: L1.current-version requires at most one current statement per account, defined as the one with no later statement, and none once the latest statement is a withdrawal; this attribute exposes that fact directly. L1.hole.deletion-reversal forbids treating a report received after a withdrawal as resuming the record, so this attribute must foreclose currency from the withdrawal's own moment forward. And L1.owner-standing's extended second sentence requires an account to have no standing when its owner has none; since 'current' is this job's compiled answer to 'does this account have standing now,' that requirement must be produced here, by referencing the owning customer's own withdrawal state, rather than left to a must-hold invariant with no derivation behind it.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible once every account statement has a known effective_from to order it against the others, a known is_withdrawal value, and (for the owner-cascade branch) a resolvable owning_customer_number whose customer entity's own is_withdrawal history is known. Assumes owning_customer_number is constant across an account's own statements unless a new account statement changes it, since whether a customer-only change reversions the account's own statements is L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account, left open. The withdrawal, reversal-foreclosure, and owner-cascade branches are not yet exercised by this job: every statement it currently produces has is_withdrawal false for both entities (see the is_withdrawal attributes), because the sources that could set it true remain deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time. Should a report ever be received after a withdrawal, this rule reads it as not resuming the record, matching trade-lifecycle's monotonic treatment of the same hole for a trade's withdrawn flag; if the business answers L1.hole.deletion-reversal to allow resumption, this derivation must be revisited.
attributes.review_trigger: zero or more than one statement of the same account_number is flagged current, or a statement with is_withdrawal true is flagged current

attributes.name: is_withdrawal

derivation.rule: false for every statement produced by raw.customer_mgmt_action, whose action_type vocabulary (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, CLOSEACCT) names no withdrawal action, and false for every statement produced by the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, whose anchored fields (status_id, tax_status_id) carry no withdrawal signal of any kind; true for a statement produced by an account CDC record whose cdc_flag is D, per the deferred handoff below, since L1.deletion-withdraws holds that such a report withdraws the brokerage's assertion of the account from its own moment rather than stating an ordinary change; false for one whose cdc_flag is I or U, an ordinary insert or update. An account CDC record whose cdc_flag is outside the anchored {I, U, D} vocabulary is not read as false by this rule: per L1.unknown-codes, that record is held for review and no fact, including is_withdrawal, is derived from it at all, so this attribute is not populated for it rather than defaulting to false.

attributes.necessity: L1.deletion-withdraws requires the model to distinguish a withdrawal report from an ordinary statement so that current-ness, as-of answers, and standing-fact content can each treat it differently as the clause requires; this attribute is that distinction, carried per statement.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible for statements sourced from raw.customer_mgmt_action or ce.account_changes, neither of which can express a withdrawal at all (the first has no such action_type, the second no such field), so is_withdrawal is always determinable as false for both. L1.constructed-scenarios' withdrawal exception would let a labeled scenario carry a withdrawal of an account the records do not have, but ce.account_changes as anchored (account_id, action_at, status_id, tax_status_id, provenance) carries no field that could signal one; exercising that exception for this job would need a different labeled source. Not yet exercisable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account CDC record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; until it is undeferred, this job produces no statement with is_withdrawal true.
attributes.review_trigger: the change-effective-time hole is resolved and the deferred cdc_flag handoff can be promoted from deferred to candidate, or a statement is found with an indeterminate is_withdrawal value

attributes.name: owning_customer_number

derivation.rule: When a statement's own source supplies no owning-customer value (as ce.account_changes does not), L1.omitted-facts-stand holds that a constructed change which does not mention the owner leaves the owner as it last stood: owning_customer_number equals the value carried by this account's immediately preceding statement. L1.identity holds that a change produces a new dated statement about the same account, not a different one, and L1.history holds that a later statement sits beside the earlier one rather than overwriting it, so 'this account's immediately preceding statement' is well defined. A constructed change sourced from ce.account_changes always has a previous statement to carry the owner from, because L1.constructed-scenarios' authorized clarification forbids a constructed scenario from introducing an account the brokerage does not have — it only changes something the received records already know — which inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account checks directly. The carried-forward derivation does not apply to a withdrawal statement (is_withdrawal = true): a withdrawal asserts no standing at all, per L1.deletion-withdraws, so it carries no owner forward either; owning_customer_number is null for such a statement, licensed only by is_withdrawal = true, exactly as status and tax_treatment are.

attributes.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing, and L1.statement-content names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account statement carries; this attribute names which customer that is so the customer's as-of statement can be looked up for the same moment. Where a statement's source does not supply this fact directly, this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history. L1.deletion-withdraws requires that a withdrawal assert no standing at all, and 'which customer owns it' is one of L1.statement-content's three standing facts; this attribute must therefore be absent on a withdrawal exactly as status and tax_treatment are, not asserted as a fact the record no longer has.
attributes.note: Non-null for every non-withdrawal statement, checked by inv.account_owner_matches_producing_source's non-withdrawal branch; null for a statement whose is_withdrawal is true, since a withdrawal asserts no standing fact at all, including who owns the account.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible for whatever account statements exist; whether a change to the customer alone produces a new account statement carrying this same value is unresolved. The carried-forward derivation is credible while a change that does not mention the owner is understood to leave the owner unchanged rather than unknown; if the business intends otherwise, this derivation must be revisited. No source this job reads today produces a withdrawal statement, so the null branch is not yet exercised; once raw.account_cdc is undeferred, its own c_id handoff must read only I/U rows for this attribute, never a D row, matching the restriction already required of the ca_st_id handoff.
attributes.review_trigger: a non-withdrawal account statement's owning_customer_number does not match any customer_number known to the customer entity, a constructed change is recorded as an account's first statement with no owning_customer_number determinable by this derivation, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null owning_customer_number

attributes.name: status
attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. A withdrawal neither opens nor closes an account, per L1.deletion-withdraws, so it must not populate this attribute either.
attributes.note: Non-null for every non-withdrawal statement, checked by inv.account_statement_has_content; null for a statement whose is_withdrawal is true, since L1.deletion-withdraws holds that a withdrawal creates nothing and neither opens nor closes an account, so it must never be read as open or closed.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its open/closed fact directly, or entails it through a stated code meaning: the historical action file entails it through the anchored meaning of action_type (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT: open; CLOSEACCT: closed), the labeled constructed scenario supplies it directly through status_id, and an incremental account change record supplies it directly through ca_st_id though its effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time). A cdc_flag='D' row on that incremental source is a withdrawal, not an update, per L1.deletion-withdraws; once undeferred, this handoff must read ca_st_id only from I/U rows, never from a D row, so this attribute is never populated from a withdrawal. No source this job reads today produces a withdrawal statement, so the null branch is not yet exercised.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement is recorded with no determinable open/closed fact from a source that is expected to supply or entail one, or the business amends L1.closed-account-activity, or states that a recorded action revises a closure, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null status

attributes.note: Non-null for every non-withdrawal statement (directly supplied or carried forward), checked by inv.account_statement_has_content; null for a statement whose is_withdrawal is true, since a withdrawal asserts no standing to carry forward or otherwise.

attributes.name: provenance
attributes.necessity: the clause requires a constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears; this attribute carries that label on the account statement so it is never mistaken for a received record.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the only anchored constructed-scenario source for this job is account-level; no equivalent labeled source exists yet for customer statements.

handoffs.necessity: L1.identity requires the customer's own number as its identity; this file's customer actions (NEW, UPDCUST, INACT) carry c_id as the brokerage's customer number on each such record.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_id values in this file are the brokerage's real customer numbers and not reused for different customers.
handoffs.review_trigger: a c_id value in this file is found reassigned to a different customer

handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while action_ts records the moment the brokerage considers the change to have taken effect, not merely when it was received into this file.
handoffs.review_trigger: action_ts is found to record only receipt time, not effective time

This is the checkable form of L1.deletion-withdraws' 'a question asked as of that moment or later has no answer for that record, rather than an older one,' bounded on its resuming side by L1.hole.deletion-reversal.
invariants.necessity: L1.as-of defines the as-of answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment, which is unique only if statements are ordered and non-overlapping; L1.deletion-withdraws requires that once a withdrawal has occurred at or before the queried moment, the as-of question has no answer at all rather than the withdrawal, an older statement, or a later ordinary statement standing in for one -- the last of which L1.hole.deletion-reversal forbids until answered.

invariants.statement: For any account_number and moment T: if the account has an as-of answer at T, the customer entity has an as-of answer for that account's owning_customer_number at the same moment T, and vice versa -- if the customer has no as-of answer at T (whether because T precedes its first statement, because its latest statement at or before T is a withdrawal, or because a withdrawal of it has occurred at or before T under the reversal-foreclosure reading of L1.hole.deletion-reversal), the account has no as-of answer at T either. The account's as-of answer is never half an answer with the owner's part missing, per L1.owner-standing's 'an account has no standing at a moment when its owner has none.' This invariant is now the direct check of the same rule logical.account.is_current's own derivation compiles for the current-moment case (the owner-cascade branch of that derivation), generalized here to arbitrary T using the same effective_from-ordered reasoning the as-of invariants in sg.history-asof already use; it does not introduce the cascade on its own.

Because logical.account.is_current's derivation now produces this same cascade for the current-moment case directly, this invariant checks that compiled behavior rather than asserting a requirement with nothing behind it.

invariants.statement: When a customer statement is a withdrawal (is_withdrawal = true) and one or more accounts have that customer as their owning_customer_number and would otherwise carry a standing at or after the withdrawal's effective moment, each such account is reported for review, naming the account, the withdrawn customer, and the withdrawal's effective moment. When an account's owning_customer_number, or the is_withdrawal value of the customer that owning_customer_number names, cannot be resolved (for example because the handoff that would supply it is still deferred), that account is itself reported as unevaluable for this check, naming the account and which input could not be resolved, rather than passed over as though the condition were false. This reports, rather than fails, L1.deletion-withdraws' 'because a customer that still owns accounts is one the brokerage may not have meant to withdraw, the withdrawal is reported for review.'
invariants.necessity: L1.deletion-withdraws requires that withdrawing a customer who still owns standing accounts be handed to the business rather than silently resolved either way, using the same reporting mechanism L1.closed-account-activity introduced for a trade placed on a closed account; this invariant is the direct, deterministic surfacing of exactly those rows. Because both of its inputs (an account's owning_customer_number and that customer's is_withdrawal) can be genuinely unresolvable independently of each other -- the account-side and customer-side CDC handoffs are deferred separately and need not be undeferred together -- the invariant must also state what it does when it cannot evaluate its own condition, per L2-FORMAT.md's requirement that an absent input be a separate reported case rather than a quiet pass.

invariants.statement: Every candidate-sourced statement of a customer that is not itself a withdrawal (is_withdrawal = false) carries a non-null status and a non-null tier; such a non-withdrawal statement without either is content-free and fails L1.statement-content. A withdrawal statement (is_withdrawal = true) carries neither status nor tier, since it asserts no standing at all, and is not content-free under this invariant for that reason.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a dated statement to carry the enumerated standing facts, not merely exist as an empty shell; this invariant is the direct check that status and tier are populated on every candidate-sourced statement, whether supplied directly by the source or carried forward under L1.omitted-facts-stand when the producing action omits the field. L1.deletion-withdraws requires that a withdrawal report carry no standing, so a withdrawal statement is excepted from this content requirement rather than being read as an empty shell.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the historical action file: NEW and UPDCUST carry c_tier directly, and INACT omits it, so tier is carried forward from the customer's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand; status is entailed by the anchored action_type meaning on every one of NEW, UPDCUST, and INACT. Does not yet hold for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that record's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time) and its content handoffs remain deferred; nor does the withdrawal exception have any statement to except yet, since no source this job reads today can produce one.
invariants.review_trigger: a customer statement from a source expected to supply or entail status or tier carries neither and its is_withdrawal is false, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null status or tier

invariants.statement: Every candidate-sourced statement of an account that is not itself a withdrawal (is_withdrawal = false) carries a non-null status and a non-null tax_treatment; such a non-withdrawal statement without either is content-free and fails L1.statement-content. A withdrawal statement (is_withdrawal = true) carries neither status nor tax_treatment, since it neither opens nor closes an account and asserts no standing at all, and is not content-free under this invariant for that reason.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a dated statement to carry the enumerated standing facts, not merely exist as an empty shell; this invariant is the direct check that status and tax_treatment are populated on every candidate-sourced statement, whether supplied directly by the source or carried forward under L1.omitted-facts-stand when the producing action omits the field. L1.deletion-withdraws requires that a withdrawal neither open nor close an account and assert no standing, so a withdrawal statement is excepted from this content requirement rather than being read as an empty shell.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the historical action file: NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT carry ca_tax_st directly, and CLOSEACCT omits it, so tax_treatment is carried forward from the account's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand; status is entailed by the anchored action_type meaning on every one of NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT. Also holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, which carries both status_id and tax_status_id directly on every row. Does not yet hold for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that record's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time) and its content handoffs remain deferred; nor does the withdrawal exception have any statement to except yet, since neither of this job's currently-projectable sources (raw.customer_mgmt_action, ce.account_changes) can produce one.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement from a source expected to supply or entail status or tax_treatment carries neither and its is_withdrawal is false, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null status or tax_treatment

invariants.statement: No logical.account.status or logical.account.tax_treatment value is ever populated by a handoff sourced from a withdrawal report. For status: the action_type -> status handoff never fires for a withdrawal because raw.customer_mgmt_action's action_type vocabulary names no withdrawal action, the ce.account_changes.status_id -> status handoff never fires for a withdrawal because that source carries no withdrawal signal, and the deferred ca_st_id -> status handoff must read only I/U rows once undeferred, never a D row. For tax_treatment: the ce.account_changes.tax_status_id -> tax_treatment handoff never fires for a withdrawal for the same reason, and the deferred ca_tax_st -> tax_treatment handoff must likewise read only I/U rows once undeferred. This is the checkable form of L1.deletion-withdraws' 'it neither opens nor closes an account' and its broader 'creates nothing', and the exact parallel of inv.account_statement_never_created_by_activity for L1.closed-account-activity's 'no trade creates a statement.' The third L1.statement-content fact, which customer owns the account, is covered the same way by inv.account_owner_matches_producing_source's own withdrawal exception in sg.owner-standing, since owning_customer_number is that group's more specific member.
invariants.necessity: L1.deletion-withdraws requires that a withdrawal neither open nor close an account and create nothing; since status and tax_treatment are this job's other two L1.statement-content facts for an account besides ownership, the direct, deterministic check of that requirement is that neither value ever traces to a withdrawal report, whether by direct handoff or by being read as though it opened, closed, or re-taxed the account.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while this job's only status- and tax_treatment-populating handoffs remain the candidate ones named above (none sourced from a withdrawal-carrying field) plus the deferred ca_st_id and ca_tax_st handoffs, whose own notes now require them to skip D rows once undeferred. Not yet exercisable end to end, since no source this job reads today can produce a withdrawal statement at all, pending L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: a logical.account statement produced from a cdc_flag = 'D' row, or from any other withdrawal report, is found with a non-null status or a non-null tax_treatment

invariants.statement: Every account statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes that is not itself a withdrawal names an account_number that already has an earlier statement sourced from a received record; a constructed change never introduces an account the brokerage does not have. A withdrawal-labeled scenario row is excepted, per L1.constructed-scenarios' narrow exception, since under L1.deletion-withdraws such a report asserts nothing and brings nothing into being; today, however, ce.account_changes carries no field distinguishing a withdrawal row from an ordinary one (see logical.account.is_withdrawal), so every row from this source is a non-withdrawal row and this exception is not yet exercised.
invariants.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios' authorized clarification states a constructed scenario changes something the received records already know and never introduces a customer, account, or trade the brokerage does not have, except for a withdrawal, which introduces nothing at all under L1.deletion-withdraws; this invariant is the direct check of that narrowed requirement for ce.account_changes. It is also what guarantees that logical.account.owning_customer_number's carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation always has a previous statement to carry from for a non-withdrawal constructed change.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while every constructed scenario used to test this job's rules is authored against an account already present in the received records, per the authorized clarification of L1.constructed-scenarios; the withdrawal exception is credible once a labeled source exists that can mark a row as a withdrawal, which ce.account_changes as anchored does not yet do.
invariants.review_trigger: a constructed account-change row's account_id has no earlier statement sourced from a received record and the row is not a withdrawal, or a withdrawal-labeled row is rejected for lacking a preceding statement

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced customer statement produced by a historical action, status equals the anchored meaning of that action's action_type (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive); once an incremental customer change record's content handoffs are undeferred, status for a statement it produces equals that record's own c_st_id value.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer statement to carry whether the customer is active or inactive; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that the status this job hands off actually equals what its producing source states, under L1.history's requirement that the action be that statement's own producing change, rather than some other statement's value being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while the anchored action_type_meanings correctly and exhaustively state NEW and UPDCUST as active and INACT as inactive; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: a customer statement's status does not equal the anchored meaning of its producing action's action_type, or, once undeferred, does not equal its producing record's c_st_id

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced customer statement whose producing action carries c_tier (NEW, UPDCUST), tier equals that row's c_tier; for one whose producing action omits it (INACT), tier equals the value carried by the customer's immediately preceding statement, per L1.omitted-facts-stand.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer statement to carry the customer's tier; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that tier equals its producing row's own value where supplied, or the previous statement's value where the row omits it under L1.omitted-facts-stand, rather than some other statement's tier being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds for statements sourced from the historical action file, where NEW and UPDCUST carry c_tier directly and INACT's carried-forward value can be checked against the customer's immediately preceding statement; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: a customer statement's tier does not equal its producing row's c_tier where carried, or does not equal the immediately preceding statement's tier where the row omits it

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced account statement produced by a historical action, status equals the anchored meaning of that action's action_type (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT: open; CLOSEACCT: closed); for one produced by a labeled constructed scenario row, status equals that row's own status_id.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that the status this job hands off actually equals what its producing source states, whether a historical action interpreted under L1.history or a constructed scenario's own status_id under L1.constructed-scenarios, rather than some other statement's value being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while the anchored action_type_meanings correctly and exhaustively state NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT as open and CLOSEACCT as closed, and while ce.account_changes.status_id states the scenario's asserted status directly; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement's status does not equal the anchored meaning of its producing action's action_type, or does not equal its producing constructed row's status_id

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced account statement whose producing row carries a tax-treatment value directly (a historical action's ca_tax_st on NEW, ADDACCT, or UPDACCT, or a constructed scenario row's tax_status_id), tax_treatment equals that value; for one whose producing historical action omits it (CLOSEACCT), tax_treatment equals the value carried by the account's immediately preceding statement, per L1.omitted-facts-stand.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account statement to carry its tax treatment; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that tax_treatment equals its producing row's own value where supplied directly, or the previous statement's value where a historical action omits it under L1.omitted-facts-stand, rather than some other statement's tax treatment being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds for statements sourced from the historical action file, where NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT carry ca_tax_st directly and CLOSEACCT's carried-forward value can be checked against the account's immediately preceding statement, and for statements sourced from ce.account_changes, which carries tax_status_id directly on every row; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement's tax_treatment does not equal its producing row's directly supplied value, or does not equal the immediately preceding statement's tax_treatment where the producing action omits it

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced account statement that is not itself a withdrawal (is_withdrawal = false) whose producing historical action carries c_id, owning_customer_number equals that action's c_id; for one produced by a constructed scenario row, which carries no owner field, owning_customer_number equals the value carried by the account's immediately preceding statement, per L1.omitted-facts-stand. A withdrawal statement (is_withdrawal = true) carries no owning_customer_number at all, since it asserts no standing fact, including who owns the account.
invariants.necessity: L1.owner-standing and L1.statement-content require an account statement to name the customer who owns it; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that owning_customer_number equals its producing historical action's own c_id where supplied, or the previous statement's value where a constructed scenario row omits it under L1.omitted-facts-stand, rather than some other statement's owner being substituted. L1.deletion-withdraws requires that a withdrawal assert no standing, including ownership, so a withdrawal statement is excepted from this requirement rather than being checked against a producing source's c_id or a carried-forward value.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds for statements sourced from the historical action file, whose account actions (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, CLOSEACCT) all carry c_id directly, and for statements sourced from ce.account_changes, whose carried-forward value can be checked against the account's immediately preceding statement, guaranteed to exist by L1.constructed-scenarios and inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; nor does the withdrawal exception have any statement to except yet, since no source this job reads today can produce one.
invariants.review_trigger: a non-withdrawal account statement's owning_customer_number does not equal its producing historical action's c_id, does not equal the immediately preceding statement's owning_customer_number where a constructed row omits the owner, or a statement with is_withdrawal true carries a non-null owning_customer_number

invariants.statement: For every raw.customer_mgmt_action row this job consumes, action_type is one of the codes chain/anchors/sources-v1.json's action_type_meanings names (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, UPDCUST, CLOSEACCT, INACT); a row carrying any other value is reported as a violation naming the row and its action_type, and nothing is derived from it. This invariant only reports the row and the code; it says nothing about what happens to the record afterward.
invariants.necessity: L1.unknown-codes requires that a report carrying a code the brokerage's fixed vocabulary does not name is held for review and never interpreted, defaulted, or dropped, and that every job report such a record as a violation naming the record and the code. This job consumes raw.customer_mgmt_action rows, whose action_type it reads to populate customer and account status; this invariant is the direct, deterministic check that a row outside the anchored action_type vocabulary is reported rather than silently interpreted, defaulted, or dropped. Whether ce.account_changes.status_id carries any vocabulary at all is this model's one open question (see questions_for_authority); until it is answered, this invariant does not check that field.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while chain/anchors/sources-v1.json's action_type_meanings remains the exhaustive, correct naming of raw.customer_mgmt_action's action_type codes.
invariants.review_trigger: a raw.customer_mgmt_action row carries an action_type outside {NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, UPDCUST, CLOSEACCT, INACT}

invariants.statement: Every logical.account statement is produced by an anchored customer management action row (raw.customer_mgmt_action), an incremental account change record (raw.account_cdc, whose own handoffs into logical.account remain deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time), or a labeled constructed scenario row (ce.account_changes); no logical.account statement is ever produced by a trade report or a holding-history report. This is the checkable form of L1.closed-account-activity's 'activity never reopens an account: no trade creates a statement.'
invariants.necessity: L1.closed-account-activity requires that activity never reopens an account because no trade creates a statement; L1.identity and L1.history require that every account statement be a new dated statement about the same account, kept beside the earlier ones, produced by a change to the account itself. This job's handoffs into logical.account are drawn only from raw.customer_mgmt_action, raw.account_cdc, and ce.account_changes; this invariant is the direct, deterministic check that no statement instead traces to a trade or holding report, which would silently reopen or amend a closed account's history through activity rather than through a recorded change to the account.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while this job's only producing sources for a logical.account statement remain raw.customer_mgmt_action, raw.account_cdc, and ce.account_changes; this job does not read raw.trade_cdc or raw.holding_history at all, so no statement can trace to either today.
invariants.review_trigger: a logical.account statement is found whose producing source is a trade report or a holding-history report rather than raw.customer_mgmt_action, raw.account_cdc, or ce.account_changes

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: Every source this job reads through a raw feed that reports a customer or account carries its own identity handoff into the customer_number or account_number attribute, typed with the identity mutation role, giving each entity the persistent, non-identity-changing value L1.identity requires. Because a versioned entity's statements must also be kept beside one another and be orderable for as-of resolution, this group also covers the entity-shape-level portion of L1.history and L1.as-of: the historical action file's own action_ts handoff makes both entities projectable as dated, ordered statements now; the incremental CDC files carry the same identity values but supply no effective moment of their own, so their identity handoffs into these versioned entities are deferred. The labeled constructed account scenario's own identity handoff is covered under sg.constructed-scenarios instead, since it is the more specific claim about that source. L1.identity also names a trade number, out of this job's scope (see job:trade-lifecycle). The attribute-level effective_from population and ordering invariants are covered by sg.history-asof; the current-flag mechanics by sg.current-version.

For every statement whose source carries its own moment of change (the historical action file's action_ts), effective_from is populated and the no-overlap and unique-answer invariants hold over it, satisfying L1.history's 'kept, with the moment it took effect' and L1.as-of's 'the latest one that took effect at or before it.' The unique-answer invariants now also state L1.deletion-withdraws' amendment directly: an as-of question at or after a withdrawal has no answer, rather than the withdrawal or an older statement standing in for one, using the is_withdrawal flag sg.current-version defines; and, per L1.hole.deletion-reversal, the no-answer bound holds from the withdrawal's own moment forward even across a later, ostensibly ordinary statement, so a report received after a withdrawal is never read as resuming the record. The labeled constructed account scenario's own effective_from handoff (action_at) is covered under sg.constructed-scenarios instead, since it is the more specific claim about that source. Incremental CDC records carry no moment of their own (a batch date is not an effective moment, per L1.hole.change-effective-time), so no effective_from handoff is created from them.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time. The no-answer-on-withdrawal behavior the unique-answer invariants now state is fully expressed, but unexercised: this job produces no statement with is_withdrawal true today, because the sources that could carry a withdrawal signal (raw.customer_cdc.cdc_flag, raw.account_cdc.cdc_flag) supply no effective-time handoff of their own and stay deferred under the same hole. Also bounded by L1.hole.deletion-reversal: the reversal-foreclosure reading these invariants state (a report after a withdrawal never resumes the record) is this job's own reading of what the hole's 'until answered' sentence licenses, not an answer to the hole itself, and must be revisited if the business answers otherwise.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The is_current flag, true for exactly the statement of a customer or account with no later statement and false for every other, together with the single-current invariants, is a direct restatement of L1.current-version's amended requirement: at most one current statement per customer and per account, exactly one while the record stands, and none once its latest statement is a withdrawal. The is_withdrawal flag is what lets is_current express that amendment: a withdrawal statement is never itself current, computed_within_entity for every statement this job currently produces (false for every raw.customer_mgmt_action- and ce.account_changes-sourced statement, since neither source's vocabulary or fields carry a withdrawal signal), and, once undeferred, from the matching CDC source's cdc_flag = 'D'. Both is_current rules are now also bounded so that a statement dated at or after a withdrawal of the same record is never treated as current, foreclosing currency from the withdrawal's own moment forward rather than only at the withdrawal statement itself, per L1.hole.deletion-reversal's 'until answered, no job may treat a report received after a withdrawal as resuming the record.' The account's is_current additionally incorporates the owner-standing cascade directly: an account statement is never current if its owning customer carries a withdrawal at or before that statement's own moment, which is where L1.owner-standing's extended second sentence is actually compiled, rather than left to sg.owner-standing's must-hold invariant with nothing producing it. This determination depends on every statement's effective_from being known; where a statement's only source is an incremental CDC file, its order relative to the customer's or account's other statements is not yet resolvable, so its current-ness cannot yet be determined either.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time. The none-once-withdrawn behavior, the reversal-foreclosure bound, and the owner-cascade bound are all fully expressed by is_current's derivation rules and the single-current invariants, but unexercised: every statement this job currently produces has is_withdrawal false for both entities, because the only sources that could set it true (raw.customer_cdc.cdc_flag, raw.account_cdc.cdc_flag) remain deferred under the same hole. Also bounded by L1.hole.deletion-reversal: the reversal-foreclosure reading this group's is_current rules now state is this job's own resolution of what the hole's 'until answered' sentence licenses (a monotonic, non-resuming reading, matching trade-lifecycle's treatment of the same hole), not an answer to the hole itself; should the business answer the hole to allow resumption, both rules must be revisited.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: Every non-withdrawal account statement sourced from a feed that itself supplies the account's own effective moment carries the identity of its owning customer: directly, from the historical action file's own c_id (the incremental account CDC file's own c_id handoff is deferred pending its own effective-time hole, and must skip D rows once undeferred); and, for a statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, which carries no owner field of its own, from this same attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation under L1.omitted-facts-stand, which holds that a constructed change not mentioning the owner leaves it as it last stood. A withdrawal statement carries no owning_customer_number at all, per L1.deletion-withdraws, checked by inv.account_owner_matches_producing_source's own withdrawal exception and inv.withdrawal_never_reaches_account_status's note that this is the same treatment given status and tax_treatment. L1.identity and L1.history make 'the account's immediately preceding statement' well defined, and L1.constructed-scenarios together with inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account guarantee that a preceding statement exists to carry from. The owner-standing cascade this group covers — L1.owner-standing's extended second sentence, that an account has no standing at a moment when its owner has none — is now produced, not merely asserted: logical.account.is_current's own derivation (member of sg.current-version) computes false for an account statement dated at or after its owning customer's withdrawal, and inv.account_asof_carries_customer_asof is the direct check of that same rule generalized to arbitrary T. inv.customer_withdrawal_with_standing_accounts_reported covers the clause's reporting sentence: a customer withdrawn while still owning standing accounts is surfaced for the business's review rather than silently resolved, using the same reporting mechanism L1.closed-account-activity introduced, and states its own behavior when its inputs cannot be evaluated rather than passing over them silently. L1.statement-content additionally names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account statement carries, which this same attribute satisfies. The inv.account_owner_matches_producing_source invariant additionally checks that owning_customer_number equals what its producing source states, directly or by carry-forward, for every non-withdrawal statement, rather than merely being non-null.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account; also bounded by L1.hole.change-effective-time (the incremental account CDC file's owner handoff remains deferred pending its own effective moment). The owner-standing cascade's producing derivation lives on logical.account.is_current in sg.current-version, not in this group; this group's own members check that compiled behavior rather than compile it. The cascade and the reporting invariant are fully expressed but unexercised for the same reason as sg.current-version's gap: no customer statement this job currently produces has is_withdrawal true, so no account has yet been observed losing standing through its owner's withdrawal, or reported for one. The reporting invariant additionally has no counterexample yet naming a non-zero expected row count for it (see chain/ce/proposed/ce-withdrawn-account-v1.json's own account for why that scenario needs a labeled customer-level constructed source this job does not have); see questions_for_authority.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: For every customer statement sourced from the historical action file: tier is handed off directly from c_tier on NEW and UPDCUST rows, and carried forward from the customer's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand on INACT rows, which omit c_tier; status is derived from action_type on every one of NEW, UPDCUST, and INACT, since the anchored action_type_meanings state a status for each. Both standing facts L1.statement-content names for a customer are therefore populated for every non-withdrawal statement this source produces, by direct handoff or carry-forward; inv.customer_statement_has_content now states the same requirement narrowed to non-withdrawal statements, since a withdrawal carries no standing fact at all. For every account statement sourced from the historical action file: tax_treatment is handed off directly from ca_tax_st on NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT rows, and carried forward from the account's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand on CLOSEACCT rows, which omit ca_tax_st; status is derived from action_type on every one of NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT. Both facts L1.statement-content names for an account are therefore populated for every non-withdrawal statement this source produces, per inv.account_statement_has_content's same narrowing; the owning-customer fact it also names is covered under sg.owner-standing instead, since it is the more specific claim about that attribute. For every account statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes — the one account source with no pending effective-time hole of its own — status and tax treatment are handed off directly from that source's own status_id and tax_status_id fields, present on every row, so this fully projectable source's statements are not content-free; this source also cannot carry a withdrawal at all, so the narrowing is vacuous for it today. The incremental CDC files carry the same tier, tax-treatment, and status values but supply no effective moment of their own, so all of their content handoffs into these versioned entities remain deferred. Four value-correctness invariants (inv.customer_status_matches_producing_source, inv.customer_tier_matches_producing_source, inv.account_status_matches_producing_source, inv.account_tax_treatment_matches_producing_source) additionally check that each populated value equals what its producing source states, directly or by carry-forward, rather than merely being non-null. Of L1.closed-account-activity, this group covers the part that bears on an account statement's own content: that activity never reopens an account because no trade creates a statement, checked directly by inv.account_statement_never_created_by_activity, and that a CLOSEACCT statement's closed status, once derived, is not itself revised by later activity, since closing unwinds nothing already attributed to the account (per the action_type -> logical.account.status handoff's parallel_assumption). Of L1.deletion-withdraws, this group covers the sentence that a withdrawal neither opens nor closes an account: inv.withdrawal_never_reaches_account_status is the direct, deterministic check that no status value ever traces to a withdrawal report, the exact parallel inv.account_statement_never_created_by_activity draws for L1.closed-account-activity. The clause's other part — reporting a trade report placed on an account after its closing statement — is covered by job:trade-lifecycle under the same clause, not by this job.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time bounds the deferred CDC-sourced handoffs above, which cannot yet be projected, and is also why the withdrawal narrowing and inv.withdrawal_never_reaches_account_status are unexercised: no source this job reads today can produce a withdrawal statement.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The handoffs drawing from the labeled ce.account_changes source that are members of this group establish this account statement's identity, effective time, and constructed label: account_id populates account_number and action_at populates effective_from, satisfying L1.identity's persistent-identity requirement and L1.history/L1.as-of's dated, ordered statement requirement for this source specifically; provenance populates the account statement's own provenance field, and only ever from this source, while no raw-sourced handoff ever populates it, satisfying L1.constructed-scenarios' 'labeled... wherever it appears' and 'never mixed into the received records.' inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account now narrows its known-account requirement to non-withdrawal rows, per L1.constructed-scenarios' narrow withdrawal exception (accepted from ce.l1.withdrawal-reaches-standing): a scenario may carry a withdrawal of an account the records do not have, since such a report asserts nothing and brings nothing into being under L1.deletion-withdraws. ce.account_changes as anchored (account_id, action_at, status_id, tax_status_id, provenance) has no field that could mark a row a withdrawal, so every row from this source is a non-withdrawal row today and the exception, while correctly stated, is not yet exercised by this source. The standing facts this source's rows also carry, status_id and tax_status_id, are populated by handoffs that are members of sg.statement-content instead, since content coverage is the more specific claim owned there; this group's coverage is limited to identity, history/as-of, and labeling for this source.

holes.question: When a customer's standing changes, does every account of that customer receive a new dated statement at that same moment, or only the customer?
Does a change recorded in an incremental customer or account change file take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment?

May a withdrawal be undone? If a record is reported again after it was withdrawn, is that the same record resuming its standing, or something the brokerage must resolve first? Until answered, no job may treat a report received after a withdrawal as resuming the record.

Does this job need to know which incremental file first delivered a fact? None of this job's clauses (L1.identity, L1.history, L1.as-of, L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, L1.statement-content, L1.constructed-scenarios) ask this. Dismissed as not applicable to job:ownership-history unless the business states a clause that requires it.
